name: Billing
description: Prepaid wallets and the ledger that IS their balance. The predecessor kept a mutable Wallet.balance column beside a Transaction table -- two truths that drift, and when they drift the customer is right and you cannot prove otherwise; here wallets.balance_minor is a ROLLUP over append-only wallet_entries, so the entries are the balance and nothing may write the number (docs/logic-decisions.md #3). Amounts are integer minor units (object_money.py), so a wallet holds dollars or satoshis or a gift-card unit without special cases. hook_wallet_entries gates debits by summing the ENTRIES rather than trusting the rollup -- a gate must be authoritative, and it documents the known check-then-append race honestly rather than pretending a reserve/capture system exists. system_wallet_replenish tops up from a saved card off-session, with the safeguard the predecessor also carried and most systems skip: a MONTHLY CAP, because autopay plus one runaway metering bug is a four-figure surprise, and a cap of zero (the default) means auto top-up is simply off. Declines -- especially the authentication-required kind an off-session charge cannot satisfy -- are reported for a human to act on, never retried in a loop that gets a processor account flagged. Plans, subscriptions and the period biller are the next slice; this one is the money container they will draw on. 0.2.0 adds the recurring half: billing_plans is a price book that VERSIONS FORWARD (an invoice must forever show the price it was billed under, so a change is a new row, never a rewrite of history customers already paid against), subscriptions carry billing_mode explicitly (wallet | subscription | hybrid -- guessing the mode from whether a plan has a base price breaks the moment someone sells a zero-base plan with a real contract), and system_billing_runner closes periods into invoices. Double-billing is the failure customers never forgive, so the runner is idempotent by provenance rather than by a dedup table: a marker on the invoice means a re-run after a crash raises nothing. The status ladder climbs BOTH ways -- paying restores service, because a ladder that only descends leaves a paying customer cut off -- and cancel-at-period-end runs service to the end of the paid period rather than billing someone for time they cannot use.
